title: Risk-driven pinning and compatibility checklist for new open-model intake
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Define an actionable, auditable policy and checklist for ingesting new open models into the Redwood Model Catalog that (a) produces a deterministic compatibility score, (b) recommends or enforces version pinning based on quantified risk, and (c) integrates automated runtime sanity checks into the intake pipeline. This ticket captures the product requirements, scope decisions, and acceptance criteria needed to unblock engineering and design work for the intake UX and onboarding automation.
background: We continue to onboard community open models at a high cadence. Current intake is manual and inconsistent: some models are pinned by default while others are served unpinned. We need a reproducible policy that balances developer agility (unpinning where safe) with production risk (breakage/regression risk for customers). The policy should be transparent to downstream teams and surfaced in the Console and catalog UI.
goals: Produce a risk-scoring algorithm (deterministic, auditable) that yields a compatibility_score (0-100) and risk_category (low/medium/high)
Define default pinning behavior per risk_category and configurable overrides for enterprise customers
Specify metadata and runtime checks required for admission (unit tests, perf profile, kv-cache sanity, tokenization sanity)
Create acceptance criteria and migration/rollback rules for later unpinning decisions
out_of_scope: Full implementation of UI mockups (handled by Design ticket DES-...)
Billing and pricing changes tied to pinned vs unpinned variants
Automated re-training or fine-tuning of community models
requirements: Compatibility metadata: ingest must capture architecture, tokenizer family, sequence_length_expectation, known-incompatible-ops list, quantization_compatibility_hint, and sample_inference_cost (p99 tokens/sec)

Deterministic checks in CI: model-load-success on target runtimes (cuda, aarch64), tokenization-consistency check across 50 canonical prompts, and KV-cache warmup test across 128 and 2048 context lengths
Automated runtime smoke: a synthetic workload runner that validates latency percentiles and memory footprint on the smallest supported GPU profile
Risk scoring rulebook: weighted factors (architecture changes, custom ops, tokenizer divergence, seq-len mismatch, failed CI checks) with thresholds for low/medium/high

Pinning policy: high risk => pinned to a specific model hash and runtime variant by default; medium risk => soft-pin (serve latest compatible but store pinned baseline and enable immediate rollback); low risk => unpinned allowed with a 48h canary phase
Catalog metadata UI: show compatibility_score, risk_category, pinned_hash (if pinned), and clear guidance for customers about fallback behavior
Audit trail: all pin/unpin decisions require a recorded rationale and author; expose in model entry history and exportable CSV
Rollback criteria: automated alert and 10% traffic automatic rollback if regression signal (quality or latency) exceeds threshold within 24h of deployment
Owner and escalation path: each intake must include an owner (research/ops) and a required secondary reviewer for high-risk models
acceptance_criteria: Schema updated: model catalog ingestion schema includes all required compatibility metadata fields and example values
Risk scorer: a reproducible script (python) that consumes metadata and returns compatibility_score and risk_category. Unit tests covering edge cases included in PR
Pinning defaults: documented mapping from risk_category to pinning behavior and integrated into intake workflow (UI flag + automated enforcement)
CI checks: at least three automated runtime checks are wired into the intake pipeline and pass on a sample community model used as the canary
Console surfaces: catalog model page displays compatibility_score, risk_category, and pinned_hash; a tooltip explains implications and rollback path
Audit log: intake action produces an audit entry with author, timestamp, rationale, and resulting decision (pinned/unpinned)
Unpinning playbook: documented acceptance criteria for an unpin request including performance/quality baselines, regression test set, and staged rollout plan
Security review: security_sign_off present for models that request unpinned production exposure (boolean in the intake record)
implementation_notes: Recommend starting with a lightweight python risk scorer in infra repo and keep rules externalized in YAML for quick iteration
Design should prioritize a compact badge-style UI instead of full table to avoid overwhelming catalog entries
Work with Runtime team to select the minimal set of CI checks that are cheap (time/cost) but high signal: model_load, tokenization_consistency, kv-cache-warmup
Agree on canonical canary workload (50 prompts + 10 long-context prompts) to standardize canary pass/fail across models
Consider a phased rollout: pilot on a subset of community models for 2 weeks, collect telemetry, then widen scope
risks_and_tradeoffs: Overly conservative pinning increases operational burden for customers and delays access to improved weights
Overly permissive unpinning risks runtime regressions for downstream customers and higher support load
Running too many CI checks on intake slows throughput and raises costs—we must balance signal vs cost
Surface complexity in Console may confuse non-technical users; rely on helpful tooltips and recommended defaults
